We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Access and purpose.** “The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Before granting access, the Testing House must identify each person by name and test role and obtain the Design Owner’s written approval. Each approved person, including any external specialist, must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House is responsible for their compliance. The same approval process applies to replacements.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The Testing House may make the working copies reasonably necessary for the tests, provided digital copies are encrypted in transit and at rest and accessible only to approved personnel. It may extract the geometry necessary to design and fabricate fixtures for these tests. It must secure physical fixtures against unauthorized access. Neither the drawings, the geometry, nor any copies, extracts or fixtures may be used for another project or to develop or assist anyone in developing a competing product.”

**Closeout and verification.** “Within 30 calendar days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the Testing House must securely erase all drawings, working copies and geometry-bearing files in its custody or that of its personnel or specialists, and destroy the derivative fixtures. Within the same period, it must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier confirming completion, identifying the categories of material destroyed and the destruction dates. Independent verification satisfies the Design Owner’s audit requirement. The Testing House may retain the agreed report and measurement records if they contain no recoverable CAD geometry.”

Can your independent verifier cover specialist-held files and backup copies within 30 days? If a backup retention cycle prevents that, please propose a maximum expiry period and wording covering access, restoration and final certification.

Our verifier can reach the specialist machining shop and accredited lab within the 30-day window – both are under our control for these tests and the deletion protocol is the same. The backup cycle is the real problem; primary systems are cleared in 30 days, but encrypted backups persist on a rolling 90-day overwrite. We need a separate construct for that, plus our calibration records and the audit mechanic. Proposed replacements below.

---

**Article X – Specialist substitution (new clause).**

"To avoid delay during the test campaign, the Testing House may maintain a shortlist of pre-approved specialists (the 'Approved Specialists List'), to be agreed in writing by the Design Owner before testing starts. If a listed specialist becomes unavailable, the Testing House may engage another listed specialist without further approval, provided it notifies the Design Owner in writing within two business days of the change and supplies the new person's name, role and signed confidentiality undertaking. Any specialist not on the list remains subject to the prior written approval process in [Access and purpose]."

*Effect:* preserves the approval gate, but gives us a workable way to keep the job moving when a machinist or lab technician drops out mid-campaign. Trade-off for you: no surprise personnel, but you lose the right to veto a substitute you have already approved on the list.

---

**Article Y – Calibration records (new carve-out).**

"Notwithstanding [Closeout and verification], the Testing House and the accredited lab may retain calibration records, test results, environmental logs and the final report for a period of two years from the date of report acceptance, as required by their accreditation bodies and quality system. Such retained records must not contain recoverable CAD geometry, parametric models or tessellated meshes; only numerical measurements, dates, instrument identifiers and calibration constants. If the Design Owner requires earlier destruction, the Testing House will instead transfer the records to the Design Owner at the Design Owner's cost before destruction."

*Effect:* addresses the accreditation-driven two-year retention without giving you geometry exposure. We isolate the extracts, attest to deletion of the geometry, and keep only measurement data.

---

**Article Z – Closeout, backup expiry and verification (replacement wording).**

"**Primary systems.** Within 30 calendar days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the Testing House must securely erase all drawings, working copies, geometry-bearing files, fixture masters and CNC programs in its custody or that of its personnel, the specialist machining shop or the accredited lab, and must destroy the derivative fixtures. The Testing House's independent verifier will confirm deletion across these locations within the same 30-day window and issue a written certificate identifying the categories of material destroyed, the locations checked and the destruction dates.

**Backup media.** Where backup retention cycles prevent erasure within 30 days, drawings and geometry-bearing files held on backup media must be (i) encrypted at rest using a key held only by the Testing House, (ii) inaccessible to any personnel other than the Testing House's named backup administrator for disaster-recovery purposes only, (iii) overwritten on the normal rotation cycle and in any event deleted no later than 90 calendar days after the trigger date in the previous paragraph. During the backup-retention period the Testing House must not restore the drawings or geometry for any purpose other than verifiable system recovery. A final backup-deletion certificate covering overwrite completion must be issued within 10 calendar days after the backup expiry date.

**Calibration and report carve-out.** Article Y governs retained calibration and report records.

**Substitution of audit access.** Independent verification under this clause replaces any contractual right of on-site audit by the Design Owner. If, despite this, the Design Owner requires an on-site review, it must be by appointment, on at least 10 business days' prior written notice, during business hours, at the Testing House's own facilities, and must not extend to any shared customer site at which the Testing House is operating on the Design Owner's behalf. The Design Owner may be accompanied by one observer at the Testing House's discretion."

*Effect:* 30 days for everything we control directly; 90 days as the hard outer limit for backups with the restoration restriction and the second certificate; the unannounced-inspection problem and the shared customer site are handled in the substitution-of-audit paragraph. Trade-off for you: you give up the right to walk in, and you accept the 90-day backup tail, but you get two written certificates, named-location coverage and an enforceable no-restoration rule.

---

**Open items I need your position on before we move to final:**

1. Pre-approved specialist list – three names each side, or do you want to nominate all of them?
2. Backup overwrite cap – is 90 days acceptable, or do you need 60? Our current cycle is 90; 60 would require a change to our retention policy and additional cost.
3. The shared customer site carve-out – is the 10-business-day-notice formulation workable, or do you want the right to attend a single witnessed deletion at the Testing House's facility in lieu of any site access?
4. Calibration records – confirm that numerical measurements without geometry satisfy your protection standard, or name the specific fields you require stripped.

I will hold a markup of the consolidated draft until items 1–4 are resolved.

We can accept the 90-day backup cycle, two years of geometry-free record retention, and independent certification in place of site access. Please incorporate the following into the consolidated draft.

1. **Specialist substitutions.** The Testing House nominates the people it expects to use, and the Design Owner approves each by name, employer and role. We propose no quota. “A listed substitute may begin work in the approved role once bound by a signed undertaking with confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House must notify the Design Owner and provide the undertaking within two business days of substitution. It must revoke the outgoing person’s access when that person ceases work on the tests. Any unlisted person or change of approved role requires prior written approval.”

2. **Backup expiry.** We accept 90 calendar days from written acceptance or earlier termination. The administrator must be named, approved and bound on the same terms before gaining access. Add to Article Z: “If disaster recovery restores protected material, the Testing House must isolate it from test personnel and ordinary users, securely erase it before returning the restored system to ordinary use, and record the restoration and erasure dates for the verifier. Restoration does not restart the 90-day period. The independent verifier must issue the final certificate within 10 calendar days after that period ends, covering all backup locations, overwrite completion and any restoration and erasure.”

3. **Audit and verification.** Please keep the primary-system certificate as drafted, including the machining shop and accredited lab. Replace the entire site-review paragraph with “The Testing House must deliver both independent certificates to the Design Owner by their respective deadlines. If a certificate omits a required location, category or destruction date, or identifies an outstanding copy, the Testing House must promptly account for the omission or copy and obtain a supplemental certificate confirming closure. Independent certification satisfies the Design Owner’s audit requirement.” We need neither a site visit nor a witnessed deletion.

4. **Calibration and test records.** Numerical vibration results, environmental readings, dates, instrument identifiers and calibration constants are acceptable. A numerical coordinate table can reproduce geometry, so the content test matters. Add to Article Y: “Retained records, including the final report and its attachments, must exclude drawings, CAD views, fixture or actuator dimensions, coordinate sets, toolpaths and other data from which protected geometry can be reconstructed. The 30-day certificate must confirm that the retained records meet this condition. The two-year period runs from written acceptance or earlier termination, after which the Testing House and lab must securely erase their retained records.” We accept transfer at our cost if we request earlier destruction.

Please carry forward the encrypted working-copy provision, the fixture permission limited to these tests, and the express prohibition on reuse for another project or to develop or assist in developing a competing product.

Accepted with the refinements as drafted. Below is the consolidated text, incorporating your wording for Articles covering specialist substitution, backup expiry, audit substitution, and the calibration/records carve-out, and carrying forward the encrypted working-copy provision, the limited fixture permission and the competing-product prohibition. I have flagged one operational note at the end.

---

# Consolidated Confidentiality and Use Provisions – Vibration Test Campaign

## 1. Access and purpose

The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Before granting access, the Testing House must identify each person by name, employer and test role and obtain the Design Owner's written approval. Each approved person, including any external specialist, must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House is responsible for their compliance. The same approval process applies to unlisted replacements and to any change of approved role.

## 2. Specialist substitutions

The Testing House will nominate the people it expects to use, and the Design Owner will approve each by name, employer and role. There is no quota. A listed substitute may begin work in the approved role once bound by a signed undertaking with confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House must notify the Design Owner and provide the undertaking within two business days of substitution. It must revoke the outgoing person's access when that person ceases work on the tests. Any unlisted person, or any change of approved role for an existing person, requires prior written approval from the Design Owner.

## 3. Working copies and fixtures

The Testing House may make the working copies reasonably necessary for the tests, provided digital copies are encrypted in transit and at rest and accessible only to approved personnel. It may extract the geometry necessary to design and fabricate fixtures for these tests. It must secure physical fixtures against unauthorized access. Neither the drawings, the geometry, nor any copies, extracts or fixtures may be used for another project or to develop, or assist anyone in developing, a competing product.

## 4. Closeout, backup expiry and verification

**Primary systems.** Within 30 calendar days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the Testing House must securely erase all drawings, working copies, geometry-bearing files, fixture masters and CNC programs in its custody or that of its personnel, the specialist machining shop or the accredited lab, and must destroy the derivative fixtures. The Testing House's independent verifier will confirm deletion across these locations within the same 30-day window and issue a written certificate identifying the categories of material destroyed, the locations checked and the destruction dates.

**Backup media.** Where backup retention cycles prevent erasure within 30 days, drawings and geometry-bearing files held on backup media must be (i) encrypted at rest using a key held only by the Testing House, (ii) inaccessible to any personnel other than the Testing House's named backup administrator (who must be approved by the Design Owner and bound on the same confidentiality and use terms before gaining access) for disaster-recovery purposes only, and (iii) overwritten on the normal rotation cycle and in any event deleted no later than 90 calendar days after the trigger date above. If disaster recovery restores protected material, the Testing House must isolate it from test personnel and ordinary users, securely erase it before returning the restored system to ordinary use, and record the restoration and erasure dates for the verifier. Restoration does not restart the 90-day period. The independent verifier must issue the final certificate within 10 calendar days after that 90-day period ends, covering all backup locations, overwrite completion and any restoration and erasure.

**Delivery of certificates.** The Testing House must deliver both independent certificates to the Design Owner by their respective deadlines. If a certificate omits a required location, category or destruction date, or identifies an outstanding copy, the Testing House must promptly account for the omission or copy and obtain a supplemental certificate confirming closure. Independent certification satisfies the Design Owner's audit requirement. The Design Owner has no right of on-site inspection or witnessed deletion in respect of these tests.

## 5. Calibration and test records

Retained records, including the final report and its attachments, must exclude drawings, CAD views, fixture or actuator dimensions, coordinate sets, toolpaths and other data from which protected geometry can be reconstructed. Numerical vibration results, environmental readings, dates, instrument identifiers and calibration constants are acceptable provided they do not, alone or in combination, permit geometry reconstruction. The 30-day certificate must confirm that the retained records meet this condition.

The Testing House and the accredited lab may retain calibration records, test results, environmental logs and the final report for a period of two years from written acceptance or earlier termination, as required by their accreditation bodies and quality system. If the Design Owner requires earlier destruction, the Testing House will instead transfer the records to the Design Owner at the Design Owner's cost before destruction. On expiry of the two-year period, the Testing House and lab must securely erase their retained records and confirm deletion in a short close-out notice to the Design Owner.

---

**Operational note for your awareness.** The disaster-recovery clause assumes a single named backup administrator on our side. If your approval process for that administrator takes longer than the 90-day clock (e.g., if the administrator changes mid-cycle and we have to re-nominate), we will need your prompt response to avoid the protected material being held beyond 90 days by operation of our rotation policy. Could you commit to a five-business-day turnaround on backup-administrator approval so the clock can run cleanly?

If that is acceptable, this is the final form from our side and I am ready to proceed to execution.

We accept the consolidated text with the following addition to the backup-media paragraph.

“The Design Owner must approve or decline a backup-administrator nomination in writing within five business days after receiving the nominee’s name, employer, role and signed confidentiality and use undertaking. Access requires affirmative written approval. A change of administrator or a pending nomination does not extend the 90-calendar-day deletion deadline.”

With that addition, the text is agreed for execution.

The addition to the backup-media paragraph is accepted as drafted. The five-business-day turnaround on administrator nominations is workable on our side, and the confirmation that a pending nomination does not extend the 90-day clock is the right construction.

The consolidated text is now final and agreed. We are ready to proceed to execution.

For operational sequencing only: I will submit the initial backup-administrator nomination (together with the test-personnel nominations) within five business days of execution so the 90-day clock runs cleanly against our next scheduled rotation window.

[END]
